top.title: PRIVATE JETS: Calls grow for tougher sanctions against erring operators
top.description: By Dickson Omobola Experts in the aviation sector have called for stricter oversight of private and charter aircraft operators in the country and urged relevant agencies to strengthen flight surveillance, improve information-sharing and impose stiffer sanctions on operators found violating aviation regulations. The experts raised concerns over regulatory enforcement following two recent serious incidents involving private aircraft: a private jet, registration number N989BC, operated by VMO Aero Ltd, which landed on a road in the Ogwashi-Uku area of Delta State, and a Challenger 604 aircraft, registration number T7-SEI, operated by Triton Aviation, whose crew reported that a door had opened in flight They particularly questioned the handling of the Asaba incident and raised concerns about the absence of a final investigation report and the enforcement actions taken against the pilot and the company responsible for managing the aircraft. One of the experts also queried the regulatory oversight of foreign-registered private jets operating in Nigeria, alleging that some operators might be exploiting their connections to influential individuals to evade regulatory requirements. Speaking to Vanguard, General Secretary of the Aviation Safety Round Table Initiative, ART, Mr Olumide Ohunayo, expressed concern that months after the Asaba incident, the authorities had yet to provide a comprehensive account of the investigation and the actions taken. “The DSS stepped in, the Ministry of Aviation, the NCAA, even the accident investigation body, yet nobody has come to tell us what they have done. Yes, there was a preliminary report, but I think we want to know what happened to that pilot. Are they not supposed to prosecute the pilot? What about the organisation that managed that aircraft? “I don’t think we should panic (both incidents). There is no red flag as far as I am concerned. There is this distinction between private and commercial operations. Yes, worldwide, commercial operations are stricter. There are more levels and layers of safety and certification that are compulsory before you can fly, compared to private operations. I think these incidents, which are also serious incidents, are meant to strengthen the regulations and processes in place.” Also speaking, aviation security expert, Group Captain John Ojikutu, retd, questioned the enforcement of regulations governing foreign-registered private aircraft operating in the country. He said: “How many of those aircraft are Nigerian-registered? They are all foreign-registered. What is the enforcement of regulation on them? top.title: UConn HC Dan Hurley toasts Huskies culture after win over Ohio State
top.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images UConn HC Dan Hurley toasts Huskies culture after win over Ohio State appeared first on ClutchPoints . The UConn Huskies passed their first real test of the season on Friday night, and Dan Hurley credited the program’s culture for carrying his team past Ohio State . No. 4 UConn pulled away in the second half for an 84-68 win over the Buckeyes in Hartford, improving to 4-0. Hurley told TNT Sports’ Andy Katz that his team’s identity showed up when it mattered. “I mean, we’re UConn. You know, like, we’re UConn, we’re dealing with some medical stuff, not just with Nik, but, you know, we just got a culture and a mindset, and I think those guys are good. You know, I liken them a lot to the Texas team that came in here last year at this time, and, you know, they got some great pieces, just take a little bit of time to gel,” Hurley said after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dan Hurley tells @TheAndyKatz @UConnMBB 's culture and mindset is what pushed them ahead against Ohio State 🔥 pic.twitter.com/tlwJwrnD9U — TNT Sports U.S. (@TNTSportsUS) November 14, 2026 The Huskies are already playing without forward Nik Khamenia, who is expected to miss several weeks with a foot injury suffered against Wagner . UConn led by double digits early, but the Buckeyes closed the first half on a 13-1 run and trailed just 42-40 at the break. Ohio State then grabbed its first lead early in the second half on a Justin Pippen 3-pointer. That is when Braylon Mullins took over . With UConn down two, Mullins scored five straight points, and Jayden Ross followed with a 3-pointer with 13:57 left. The Huskies never trailed again, outscoring the Buckeyes 42-28 in the second half. Mullins finished with a team-high 22 points and five triples before hobbling off with 6:07 remaining. Na’jai Hines added 20 points on 7-of-8 shooting, scoring 17 of them after halftime. “Well, that’s how you make up for the [Khamenia] loss. You know, we got to get more from our bigs,” Hurley said. He also wants more from his guards and his defense. “We got to have our backcourt show up and play like the best backcourt in the country, and, you know, we got to turn it up at the defensive end like we did the last 12 to 15 minutes,” he added. UConn will face a much tougher test on Wednesday when it visits No. 12 Arizona. top.title: US Flight Ground Stop: What we know about disruption
top.description: The United States has lifted a nationwide flight ground stop that lasted more than four hours, marking the longest shutdown of departing flights since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) attributed Friday’s disruption to what it described as “extraordinary circumstances” arising from a communications failure affecting air traffic control centres across the country. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident resulted from an attack, assuring that passengers and aviation personnel were safe throughout the disruption. Here are the major details of the incident. How many flights were affected? The ground stop resulted in more than 8,500 flight delays and nearly 8,000 cancellations on Friday, according to flight-tracking service FlightAware. The FAA initially announced the restriction at 3:54 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (20:54 GMT), directing that all departing flights within the United States remain grounded until further notice. More than 3,500 aircraft were airborne when the order was issued. While some were diverted to alternative airports, others continued to their intended destinations. Several hours later, the FAA began allowing limited departures, including flights from San Francisco International Airport. The agency officially reopened US airspace at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (01:15 GMT on Saturday). What happened to international flights? The disruption also affected international aviation, with flights bound for the United States from countries within the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation, known as Eurocontrol, suspended at the FAA’s request. Eurocontrol confirmed on its website that the suspension was due to technical problems affecting US aviation operations. The organisation has 42 member states, including European Union countries, the United Kingdom, Ukraine, Turkey, Israel and Morocco. Sydney Airport, Australia’s largest international airport, also grounded all US-bound flights pending further notice. Air Canada equally cancelled flights between the United States and Canada. When will normal flight operations resume? Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that the disruption would have consequences for airline operations over several days, even after the ground stop was lifted. “It’s going to take us some time to unwind what’s happened this afternoon,” he said at a news conference on Friday night. Duffy disclosed that tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports across the country, with many uncertain about where they would spend the night. Major airlines announced different recovery plans following the reopening of US airspace. Delta Air Lines and United Airlines said they were resuming operations, while American Airlines said it was working to operate as many remaining flights as possible that evening. top.title: ‘The World’s Strongest Dad’ – Keito Yamakita Heads Into World Title Fight With A New Reason To Win
top.description: Life rarely delivers a man’s two greatest desires in the exact same breath, but for Keito “Pocket Monk” Yamakita , destiny is converging on a single week. The surging Japanese martial artist is currently staring down two massive, life-altering countdowns. One leads directly to a career-defining World Title fight, while the other ticks toward the arrival of his precious firstborn child. That incredible convergence culminates at ONE SAMURAI 5 on Wednesday, November 18, when he officially challenges reigning ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion Joshua “The Passion” Pacio at EBARA WAVE Arena Ota in Tokyo. View this post on Instagram While martial arts has entirely defined Yamakita’s existence since his earliest days on the wrestling mats of Inabe in Mie Prefecture, fatherhood represents a profoundly different kind of unknown. With his wife due to give birth the very day after the World Title match, his heart is already tethered to a far greater miracle waiting just outside the Circle. Yet the 30-year-old candidly admits his sense of maturity has not fully caught up with the monumental shift ahead. Even so, he is eagerly looking forward to growing into the role the moment his son is born. The expectant father told onefc.com: “We’d wanted a child for quite a while, so more than anything I felt relieved that it had actually happened. There were worries too. “And the hundreds of days until the birth seemed so long. It felt endless, but before I knew it, it was almost here. So now I’m feeling a little restless and excited.” Photo credit: ONE Championship Fate may have perfectly aligned the dates, but “Pocket Monk” has spent a lifetime grinding toward this athletic peak. An impressive 6-1 promotional record and a brilliant five-fight winning streak delivered Yamakita to the biggest night of his professional career. Lately, though, his quiet moments reach far beyond himself, extending toward the life that follows. He added: “I’ll be a father while still competing, and I’d love my son to see me fight. That will probably be a little further down the road, but I’m really looking forward to him watching my fights.” View this post on Instagram That nervous anticipation sits alongside steady, unwavering support at home. His wife has never demanded he win a gold belt, only that he returns home in one piece. Still, a profound internal shift has altered how he approaches the grueling work ahead, and the reason is rapidly approaching. The Team We athlete continued: “I was chasing championship belts for myself. Even when I became Pancrase champion in Japan, I felt I was doing it for myself. Now I have my son to do it for as well, so that gives me even more motivation. “I went into fights wanting to give one hundred percent of what I had. Now, with my child in the picture, I feel like I can give one hundred and twenty percent—something beyond what I normally have in me.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship The Example Yamakita Wants To Set For a man standing on the precipice

top.title: Florida High captures elusive complete game in playoff rout vs Jackson
top.description: Every year the postseason rolls around, the saying goes, “win and advance.” No. 4 seed Florida State University School (9-2) did just that on Friday, beating the visiting No. 5 Andrew Jackson High School (7-4) of Jacksonville 42-6 in the FHSAA Class 2A regional quarterfinals at Mike Hickman Stadium. “I’ve seen this for this group and been excited to try to put it all together,” Florida High head coach Jarrod Hickman told the Tallahassee Democrat. “Which is what we needed to do and have to do this time of the year.” Hickman added that he wanted his team to get off to a “fast start,” something that eluded the Seminoles in their two losses this season. Most recently, in a 31-27 shortfall to James S. Rickards in the Oct. 29 regular season finale. “We pushed through adversity,” said quarterback Jayme Miller . “It was hard, but we knew what we had to do.” If one looked down, by the second quarter the Florida High Seminoles were already up 28-0 on the Jackson Tigers. Miller, a junior, tossed four touchdowns on the night. Two went to four-star wide receiver Ar’Tavian ‘Bubba’ Brown . Running back Brisyn Brown and receiver Messiah Anariva caught the others. On the ground, running back Mike Jones reached the end zone, and Brisyn Brown got him one too. Friday was the fifth time the Seminoles cracked 40 points. They average 34.4 points per game. “Lighting up the scoreboard is a big part of the game,” Miller explained. “You just got to go shot for shot. We’re playing good football, but it could be better. There are some things we got to capitalize on.” Florida High also stonewalled the Andrew Jackson Tiger offense that entered Friday averaging 26.9 points per game. Defensive back Gavin Brown notched a fumble recovery at the expense of Jackson quarterback Hans Price. Special teams also forced some turnovers. The lone score for the Tigers was a touchdown pass from Price to Malkiel Pierce. Next for Florida High is a trip to Jacksonville to face the No. 1 seed and Florida high school football powerhouse Bolles School Bulldogs (8-2) in the regional semifinals. They eliminated Freeport 49-7 on Friday. “The test is going to continue to get more challenging,” Hickman said. “And you have to be even that much sharper on the road.” It’s a rematch from the 2025 playoffs, when the Bulldogs defeated the Seminoles 51-27 in last year’s semis. The veteran was instantly assessed a flagrant foul one for unnecessarily pushing the Spurs’ big man. This sequence came soon after the Warriors’ 0-18 start against the Spurs tonight, which dug them into a major hole they needed to climb out of. top.title: Vero Beach blanks Fort Pierce Central, advances to regional semifinals
top.description: VERO BEACH — The Vero Beach High School football team extended a number of streaks with its latest victory. But given how close his team’s last two games were against Fort Pierce Central, longtime Vero Beach coach Lenny Jankowski walked off the field less concerned about a string of wins and more focused on being 1-0 in its most recent game. “Each game is independent of the other. But we knew we were in for it tonight,” Jankowski said. “(The Cobras) are a very well-coached team with some really good players. And obviously, we’re familiar with each other being in the same district. We were really just concerned with tonight and pleased with the outcome.” Vero Beach struck first with a surge late in the first half, tacked on a pair of second-half scores and never looked back en route to a 24-0 victory over Fort Pierce Central in a Region 2-6A quarterfinal Friday, Nov. 13, at Billy Livings Field at the Citrus Bowl. Vero Beach collected its eighth consecutive victory this season. The team also extended both its winning streak against the Cobras and its regional quarterfinal winning streak to 14 games. “It’s a big win and a lot of good things happened,” Jankowski said. Latravious Woods finished with two touchdown receptions, the first of which broke the ice in what was a scoreless first half to that point. The junior wide receiver got free on a corner route and hauled in a pass from Makai White for a 58-yard touchdown with 1 minute, 39 seconds remaining in the second quarter. After forcing a punt on the next Central possession, Vero Beach marched 59 yards in a matter of seconds. Synder Arbelaez capped the drive with a 26-yard field goal to put the home team ahead 10-0 at halftime. Vero Beach added to its lead late in the third quarter. Following an interception by Jeromie King, White connected with Sebastian Cabrera on a 57-yard reception down the sideline to put Vero Beach on the doorstep. Three plays later, Woods notched his second touchdown of the night after taking a wide receiver screen 10 yards into the end zone. On the previous play, Woods showed some frustration after White did not look his way. But the ball found the junior on the next snap, and he did what he does best after the catch. “Playing with Makai is great. I love playing with him,” Woods said. “He’s young, so I know I got to stay on him and keep his preparation right. I’m happy to see him grow and he’s been growing the whole season.” Woods finished with four receptions for 104 yards and four carries for 17 yards. White completed 11 of 19 passes for 214 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. With Vero Beach in command, Marc Johns put a bow on the victory in the fourth quarter. The senior athlete took a handoff to the right, cut back to the left and crossed the goal line as he was tackled for a spectacular 16-yard touchdown run with 8:44 remaining. top.title: New Canaan football makes late goal-line stand to hold off Wilton in Week 10 thriller
top.description: Jack Crowell accounted for both touchdowns in New Canaan's 16-12 win over Wilton on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Wilton High. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) WILTON - The New Canaan High football team played yet another nail-biter on Friday night, this time against Wilton at Tom Fujitani Field. This time, the Rams finished off a 16-12 victory over the Warriors, but it came down to one final defensive stand at their own goal line. New Canaan improved to 7-2 while Wilton fell to 4-5. Wilton senior Liam Smith came up with an interception of New Canaan quarterback Maddox Hoffman at the Rams' 24-yard line with 3:41 left in the game. The Warriors pushed the ball to the 10, where they had it on second-and-9 with two minutes remaining. New Canaan's defense stopped Wilton quarterback Connor Harlacher on a draw for no gain, then an incomplete pass from Harlacher brought up fourth-and-9 from the 10 with 1:13 remaining. The Warriors called for a trick play, a lineman-eligible pass from Harlacher to senior Krystian Babinski, but the Rams sniffed it out after just a 2-yard gain to squelch the home team's last gasp. As he has done time and again, New Canaan senior captain Jack Crowell came up big for his team. The Rams trailed 6-0 at halftime, but Crowell took a direct snap for a 53-yard touchdown 1:29 into the third quarter. Neel Arora's extra point put New Canaan ahead 7-6. Wilton senior captain Nicholas Mercado was in the right place at the right time when Maddox, who was in the grasp of a sack, tried to get rid of the ball. nigeria.title: Emperor, 8,000 soldiers and lesson for Nigeria
nigeria.description: I came looking for ancient soldiers and left thinking about Nigeria’s tourism potential. One thing I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures, and of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepared me for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! If you have watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there. But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to 221 BC when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that. While some people prepared for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation. The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. Above the excavation pit in Xi’an, I stood where visitors have looked down on the Terracotta Army for decades: thousands of figures, each made by hand, and still not fully unearthed. What makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over 2,000 years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974 when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army. I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world, and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. But beyond the fascinating history, what struck me most was what China has done with this discovery. This is where the story becomes particularly interesting for Nigeria. Bode said the hospital had pioneered small incision cataract excision surgery in Nigeria and trained over 40 doctors from all over the country in the procedure in the past years. nigeria.title: World Diabetes Day: High cost pushes drugs, special diets out of reach
nigeria.description: As the world marks the 2026 World Diabetes Day today, attention is once again drawn to the importance of early diagnosis, timely treatment and sustained care in preventing complications and saving lives. But for many Nigerians living with the condition, the challenge goes beyond early detection to affording medication, special diets and regular medical checks needed to manage the disease. Some patients who spoke to Weekend Trust said the rising cost of treatment had pushed them into financial hardship, forcing them to ration prescribed drugs, compromise their diets or go for days without medication. For Mrs Ngunengen Akpam, living with diabetes has become a daily struggle, not only against the disease but also against the rising cost of managing it. The burden is compounded by her responsibility to also support her diabetic mother, Mama Lydia Acka, making the cost of medication, food and routine medical care a constant source of worry for the family. Akpam told one of our correspondents that the prices of essential diabetes medications had increased considerably over the years, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the treatment prescribed by her doctors. She recalled that Metformin, one of the drugs she takes, which sold for N700 for a pack of three cards in 2015, now costs about N2,500. Similarly, Dormin, which previously sold for N700, now costs N3,500 for a pack of 10 cards, she said. “The cost of drugs has increased tremendously. I take my medication twice daily, so it is not easy. In a month, we spend so much, especially when you have another diabetic person to cater for,” she said. Medication, however, is only part of the financial burden. Akpam explained that managing diabetes also requires adherence to a carefully regulated diet, including millet, beans and vegetables, which have also become expensive. Although the price of millet had dropped from more than N1,200 to N600 per mudu during the harvest season, she said her financial circumstances still made it difficult to consistently afford the recommended food items. The experience is similar for Mrs Elahi Onu, who has lived with diabetes for 11 years and whose treatment has become a major financial responsibility for her children. Onu said her children spend at least N25,000 monthly on medication alone, while more than N60,000 goes into providing the special diet recommended for managing her condition. She listed unripe plantain, beans, vegetables, basmati rice and grains such as millet among the food items she had been advised to eat. “These special types of food are costly and drain the pockets of my children. “Sometimes there is a delay in supplies of these items to me. I will be forced to go hungry for the period or fall back to any available food,” she said. Beyond feeding and medication, Onu said she also had to contend with the cost of routine medical examinations. She disclosed that one of her prescribed medications, Triviamet, costs about N13,000 for a pack of 35 tablets

nigeria.title: Charting lasting path for Flamingos, other rising football stars
nigeria.description: On Saturday, November 7, Nigeria’s Flamingos edged out Asian giants Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco, to lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. They became the first African nation to claim the global title and placed Nigeria alongside France as the only countries to win both the men’s and women’s U-17 World Cups. The Flamingos’ male counterparts, the Golden Eaglets—with five titles—remain the most successful team in the world at that level. The victorious Flamingos returned to Nigeria on Monday, November 9, to a rousing welcome. Yet amid the national celebrations, federal cash rewards, and Senate commendations, a familiar anxiety lingers over the future of the young players. For decades, Nigeria has dominated youth tournaments, only to watch many of its brightest teenage sensations fade into obscurity. While stars like Victor Osimhen and Asisat Oshoala successfully transitioned to the global stage, countless others, hampered by poor management, unhealed injuries, or structural neglect, abandoned football altogether before their prime. Indeed, the history of Nigerian football is replete with stories of teenage sensations who sparkled at dawn with youth national teams only to fade into obscurity before noon. Thus, in spite of Nigeria’s dominance at the U-17 level, the country is yet to taste global victory at the U-20 level. The Flying Eagles, the team meant to harness the best talent from victorious U-17 squads, have managed to claim only two silver medals and one bronze since their first appearance in 1983. Similarly, only a handful of players have successfully transitioned from the U-17 to the U-20 and senior Super Eagles squads. Nduka Ugbade, Jonathan Akpoborie, Celestine Babayaro, Mikel Obi, Chinedu Obasi, Lukman Haruna, Ramon Azeez, Isaac Success and Taiwo Awoniyi are among the few who completed the full international pathway. Nigerias’ Flamingos U17 celebrating their World Cup win To ensure the 2026 Flamingos squad, and the next generation of young Nigerian athletes, don’t become cautionary tales, Nigerian football administrators must shift their focus from one-off tournament celebrations to sustainable career architecture. One of the biggest leaks in Nigerian football happens immediately after a youth tournament ends. Without a centralised database, young players return to disorganised local setups and vanish from national team radars. It is, therefore, a step in the right direction that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has promised to preserve the core of the victorious Flamingos, with 11 players still eligible for the next U-17 competition. Meanwhile, the federation stated that others would be groomed for the U-20 national team, the Falconets, and eventually the Super Falcons. nigeria.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in forfeiture case
nigeria.description: —Restricts use of document in ongoing criminal trial By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Friday admitted a Supreme Court judgment tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, in the ongoing trial of former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Godwin Emefiele, over the forfeiture of properties allegedly linked to him. However, the trial judge, Justice Rahman Oshodi, ruled that although the judgment was admissible, it could not be used for or against any of the parties in the criminal proceedings. Ruling on objections raised by the defence, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and submissions by the prosecution, led by the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, Justice Oshodi held that the document was a public document and a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision. The judge consequently admitted it as Exhibit A but restricted its use in the trial. He said: “The judgment is a public document, and it is a certified true copy of the Supreme Court decision. It would be accepted as an exhibit (in rem), but cannot be used in the case either for or against any party.” Justice Oshodi explained that the document satisfied the legal requirements for admissibility under the Evidence Act. On the defence’s objection that the prosecution tendered only the lead judgment without the separate judgments of other Supreme Court justices, the judge relied on the Court of Appeal decision in Matthias Sikiri and Others v. Nketchukwu Onyema and Others (2021) LPELR-56552(CA). He also cited Avacha and Others v. Fawole, where the Supreme Court held that the lead judgment represents the decision of the court. Addressing concerns over the use of a judgment arising from civil forfeiture proceedings in a criminal trial, Justice Oshodi said the restriction on its use had adequately addressed the issue. Citing David Itauma v. Friday Jasi, the judge said previous judgments tendered in subsequent proceedings were intended to establish what was decided in the earlier cases and not to prove the guilt or innocence of parties in the subsequent proceedings. He consequently overruled the defence objection and admitted the document. Earlier, Ojo had opposed its admission, arguing that the judgment was irrelevant to the charges against his client, incomplete without the other justices’ opinions and arose from non-conviction-based civil forfeiture proceedings. Counsel to the second defendant, A.M. Kotoye, SAN, aligned himself with the objection and urged the court to reject the document. However, Oyedepo argued that the judgment was admissible as a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision, adding that the prosecution had complied with Sections 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act. He maintained that the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not affect its admissibility, while the civil nature of the forfeiture proceedings did not make the document inadmissible. nigeria.title: JAR 2026: Stakeholders move to tackle health workforce shortages
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja Stakeholders in Nigeria’s health sector have resolved to take urgent measures to address persistent shortages and uneven distribution of healthcare workers, inadequate funding and unequal access to quality medical services, particularly in rural and underserved communities. The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the three-day 2026 Health Sector Joint Annual Review (JAR), held at the Transport Events Centre, Abuja. The review brought together representatives of federal and state governments, development partners, professional associations, civil society organisations, the private sector and other health institutions to assess progress under ongoing health sector reforms and identify priority actions to improve healthcare delivery. The communiqué, read by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ms Daju Kachollom, reaffirmed stakeholders’ commitment to addressing the country’s human resources for health crisis through the implementation of the National Human Resources for Health Programme. The programme will be supported by a dedicated management structure, an implementation work plan and a workforce retention strategy. Stakeholders also agreed to introduce targeted incentives to encourage the deployment and retention of healthcare workers in rural and underserved communities. They called for stronger collaboration with professional associations to promote equitable workforce distribution, alongside improved welfare, professional development, certification, training and supportive supervision. On healthcare financing, participants stressed the need to move beyond increased budgetary commitments to sustainable domestic financing, timely release of approved funds and more effective utilisation of available resources. They consequently resolved to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation, increase budgetary allocations to health and implement appropriate health taxation policies to support sustainable healthcare financing. The communiqué also called for stronger public financial management and accountability through improved compliance with Basic Health Care Provision Fund guidelines, digital expenditure tracking and better links between health spending and measurable service delivery outcomes. Participants emphasised that increased investment in the sector must translate into tangible improvements in healthcare access and quality. Recognising primary healthcare as the foundation of an effective health system, stakeholders resolved to accelerate efforts to make primary healthcare facilities fully functional, beginning with facilities already designated as ready for service delivery. nigeria.title: NCC introduces spectrum incentives to boost telecom investment
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has introduced a new framework offering telecommunications operators incentives linked to their spectrum licences in exchange for increased investment in network infrastructure and improved service quality. The initiative, known as the Incentive-Based Spectrum Investment Framework (IBSIF), is designed to expand network coverage, increase capacity, improve broadband access and address persistent quality-of-service challenges across the country. Announcing the framework on Thursday, the Commission said it was shifting from an approach that relied largely on revenue generated through spectrum licence fees to one that uses spectrum management as a tool for stimulating investment and delivering greater benefits to consumers. The NCC said the initiative had become necessary as rising demand for internet services continued to put pressure on existing telecommunications infrastructure, requiring operators to invest more in network expansion and capacity. According to Commission statistics, monthly data consumption in Nigeria increased from approximately 517,670 terabytes in January 2023 to 1.73 million terabytes in September 2026, representing more than a threefold increase in just over three years. It noted that Nigeria remained largely dependent on mobile networks for internet access, making sustained investment in mobile telecommunications infrastructure critical to expanding connectivity. The growing adoption of digital services, including artificial intelligence, cloud computing and online businesses, is also expected to increase demand for data and place additional pressure on existing networks. Although 4G coverage has expanded to slightly above 80 per cent of the population, the Commission said further investment was required to improve network capacity and extend broadband services to underserved communities. The situation is more challenging with 5G technology, whose population coverage stood at approximately 13 per cent as of April 2026. The NCC said accelerating 5G deployment would help meet growing demand for high-speed connectivity and more reliable digital services, but stressed that the ultimate objective was to translate infrastructure investment into tangible improvements in consumers’ experience. Under IBSIF, telecommunications operators will be encouraged to commit additional resources to network expansion, wider population coverage, increased capacity and improved service quality. In return, operators may receive appropriate incentives linked to their spectrum licences, with the benefits tied to measurable improvements in their networks. The Commission explained that operators would not receive incentives merely for making investment promises. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. nigeria.title: Global outage: Microsoft blames network change for service disruption

nigeria.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes. “While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions. “In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.” The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed. nigeria.title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a major milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying the project will open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs. Represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026, Tinubu commended Governor Bassey Otu and the people of Cross River for sustaining the project’s vision and moving it towards actualisation. The President recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving fresh impetus under Otu. Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway intended to facilitate the movement of cargo to markets across the country. Tinubu credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial challenges, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. “This is beyond a Cross River dream. It is a Nigerian project. It is a poverty breaker,” he said. President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday Tinubu stressed that the Bakassi port would complement, rather than compete with, Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in trade. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its loads on one shoulder. That shoulder will break,” he said. He argued that establishing another major maritime gateway would reduce pressure on Lagos ports, ease congestion and lower costs. “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs,” the President added. He said Nigeria had not fully exploited its coastline along the Gulf of Guinea, while neighbouring countries continued to benefit from trade that could be attracted to Nigerian ports. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would help retain regional cargo, expand access to international markets and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in maritime trade. He noted that about 90 per cent of cargo moves by sea, but Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite its economic position in West Africa. The port, he said, would help close the gap, reduce dependence on a single maritime gateway and enable the country to capture a larger share of regional commerce. The President also acknowledged the territorial and economic losses suffered by Cross River following the Bakassi Peninsula ruling and the loss of oil revenue. business.title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration. Home mining is not a profit play Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. The UConn Huskies passed their first real test of the season on Friday night, and Dan Hurley credited the program’s culture for carrying his team past Ohio State . sports.title: Florida High captures elusive complete game in playoff rout vs Jackson
sports.description: Every year the postseason rolls around, the saying goes, “win and advance.” No. 4 seed Florida State University School (9-2) did just that on Friday, beating the visiting No. 5 Andrew Jackson High School (7-4) of Jacksonville 42-6 in the FHSAA Class 2A regional quarterfinals at Mike Hickman Stadium. “I’ve seen this for this group and been excited to try to put it all together,” Florida High head coach Jarrod Hickman told the Tallahassee Democrat. “Which is what we needed to do and have to do this time of the year.” Hickman added that he wanted his team to get off to a “fast start,” something that eluded the Seminoles in their two losses this season. Most recently, in a 31-27 shortfall to James S. Rickards in the Oct. 29 regular season finale. “We pushed through adversity,” said quarterback Jayme Miller . “It was hard, but we knew what we had to do.” If one looked down, by the second quarter the Florida High Seminoles were already up 28-0 on the Jackson Tigers. Miller, a junior, tossed four touchdowns on the night. Two went to four-star wide receiver Ar’Tavian ‘Bubba’ Brown . Running back Brisyn Brown and receiver Messiah Anariva caught the others. On the ground, running back Mike Jones reached the end zone, and Brisyn Brown got him one too. Friday was the fifth time the Seminoles cracked 40 points. They average 34.4 points per game. “Lighting up the scoreboard is a big part of the game,” Miller explained. “You just got to go shot for shot. We’re playing good football, but it could be better. There are some things we got to capitalize on.” Florida High also stonewalled the Andrew Jackson Tiger offense that entered Friday averaging 26.9 points per game. Defensive back Gavin Brown notched a fumble recovery at the expense of Jackson quarterback Hans Price. Special teams also forced some turnovers. The lone score for the Tigers was a touchdown pass from Price to Malkiel Pierce. Next for Florida High is a trip to Jacksonville to face the No. 1 seed and Florida high school football powerhouse Bolles School Bulldogs (8-2) in the regional semifinals. They eliminated Freeport 49-7 on Friday. “The test is going to continue to get more challenging,” Hickman said. “And you have to be even that much sharper on the road.” It’s a rematch from the 2025 playoffs, when the Bulldogs defeated the Seminoles 51-27 in last year’s semis. sports.title: Vero Beach blanks Fort Pierce Central, advances to regional semifinals
sports.description: VERO BEACH — The Vero Beach High School football team extended a number of streaks with its latest victory. But given how close his team’s last two games were against Fort Pierce Central, longtime Vero Beach coach Lenny Jankowski walked off the field less concerned about a string of wins and more focused on being 1-0 in its most recent game. “Each game is independent of the other. But we knew we were in for it tonight,” Jankowski said. “(The Cobras) are a very well-coached team with some really good players. And obviously, we’re familiar with each other being in the same district. We were really just concerned with tonight and pleased with the outcome.” Vero Beach struck first with a surge late in the first half, tacked on a pair of second-half scores and never looked back en route to a 24-0 victory over Fort Pierce Central in a Region 2-6A quarterfinal Friday, Nov. 13, at Billy Livings Field at the Citrus Bowl. Vero Beach collected its eighth consecutive victory this season. The team also extended both its winning streak against the Cobras and its regional quarterfinal winning streak to 14 games. “It’s a big win and a lot of good things happened,” Jankowski said. Latravious Woods finished with two touchdown receptions, the first of which broke the ice in what was a scoreless first half to that point. The junior wide receiver got free on a corner route and hauled in a pass from Makai White for a 58-yard touchdown with 1 minute, 39 seconds remaining in the second quarter. After forcing a punt on the next Central possession, Vero Beach marched 59 yards in a matter of seconds. Synder Arbelaez capped the drive with a 26-yard field goal to put the home team ahead 10-0 at halftime. Vero Beach added to its lead late in the third quarter. Following an interception by Jeromie King, White connected with Sebastian Cabrera on a 57-yard reception down the sideline to put Vero Beach on the doorstep. Three plays later, Woods notched his second touchdown of the night after taking a wide receiver screen 10 yards into the end zone. On the previous play, Woods showed some frustration after White did not look his way. But the ball found the junior on the next snap, and he did what he does best after the catch. “Playing with Makai is great. I love playing with him,” Woods said. “He’s young, so I know I got to stay on him and keep his preparation right. I’m happy to see him grow and he’s been growing the whole season.” Woods finished with four receptions for 104 yards and four carries for 17 yards. White completed 11 of 19 passes for 214 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. With Vero Beach in command, Marc Johns put a bow on the victory in the fourth quarter. The senior athlete took a handoff to the right, cut back to the left and crossed the goal line as he was tackled for a spectacular 16-yard touchdown run with 8:44 remaining. sports.title: New Canaan football makes late goal-line stand to hold off Wilton in Week 10 thriller
sports.description: Jack Crowell accounted for both touchdowns in New Canaan's 16-12 win over Wilton on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Wilton High. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) WILTON - The New Canaan High football team played yet another nail-biter on Friday night, this time against Wilton at Tom Fujitani Field. This time, the Rams finished off a 16-12 victory over the Warriors, but it came down to one final defensive stand at their own goal line. New Canaan improved to 7-2 while Wilton fell to 4-5. Wilton senior Liam Smith came up with an interception of New Canaan quarterback Maddox Hoffman at the Rams' 24-yard line with 3:41 left in the game. The Warriors pushed the ball to the 10, where they had it on second-and-9 with two minutes remaining. New Canaan's defense stopped Wilton quarterback Connor Harlacher on a draw for no gain, then an incomplete pass from Harlacher brought up fourth-and-9 from the 10 with 1:13 remaining. The Warriors called for a trick play, a lineman-eligible pass from Harlacher to senior Krystian Babinski, but the Rams sniffed it out after just a 2-yard gain to squelch the home team's last gasp. As he has done time and again, New Canaan senior captain Jack Crowell came up big for his team. The Rams trailed 6-0 at halftime, but Crowell took a direct snap for a 53-yard touchdown 1:29 into the third quarter. Neel Arora's extra point put New Canaan ahead 7-6. Wilton senior captain Nicholas Mercado was in the right place at the right time when Maddox, who was in the grasp of a sack, tried to get rid of the ball. It went right to Mercado, who took it 75 yards for a touchdown and a 12-7 Warrior lead late in the third quarter. After New Canaan took advantage of a bad Wilton snap and stopped Denny Dustin in the end zone for a safety that cut Wilton's lead to 12-9 15 seconds into the fourth quarter, the Rams got good field position. New Canaan drove to the Wilton 4, where it faced a fourth-and-3. Crowell, who had run the ball on direct snaps on the previous two plays, took another run toward the right side. He pulled up short, jumped in the air and threw a pass to junior Luke Williams for a 4-yard touchdown and the lead. Arora's extra point made it 16-12 in favor of the Rams with 7:44 left in the game. Wilton punted on its next possession to pin New Canaan deep with 4:38 to play. The Rams ran the ball twice, then Hoffman rolled to his right on third down and threw toward his team's sideline. Smith caught the ball and got both feet in bounds to preserve the pick. On a third-and-9 from the New Canaan 23, Harlacher hit Dustin for a 12-yard gain and a first down at the 11 with 2:53 to play. The Warriors, who had upended Greenwich the week before, were within range of pulling off another huge win. New Canaan's defense stepped up when it had to, however, and preserved the victory. technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. Fifty-eight percent of adults 14­–39 years old who modified their use cited cost as a barrier, compared with just 20 percent of adults 65 or older who said the same. Read full article Comments

technology.description: US export controls are not stopping AI labs in China from using restricted Nvidia chips, according to a report from a former OpenAI engineer. "This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it," said DePue in a social media post . "When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern – a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model." It doesn't sound that insane. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang followed from revelations that he had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who, in 2023, founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International. That company is reportedly under investigation by US authorities for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Huang's departure coincides with a renewed push to tighten US chip export controls. House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the idea . And there are at least four bills awaiting consideration that aim to limit China's access to leading edge AI tech: the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, Match Act, and the Cloud Security Act. On Monday, US Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) cited Jensen Huang's "relationship with a suspected Chinese spy" as a justification for passing the AI Overwatch Act, which would codify the Trump administration's existing chip export controls. technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. The security firm said China-linked groups such as Vault Panda and Genesis Panda moved even faster, launching attacks within 24 hours of disclosure. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. LogicLens doesn't identify the AI models powering its service in its publicly available documentation, but AI is definitely the backbone of the system. According to LogicLens, it's using an AI system that's “Research-backed and custom designed to outperform general models like ChatGPT & even trained experts.” We’ll leave that up to anyone willing to give the tool a spin to decide, but one thing’s for certain: The world needs something. Large language models and image generation tools are increasingly being used to generate internet content slop, and not all of it is as harmless as poorly made commercials for drop-shipped garbage: Some of it is being used to craft very convincing misinformation. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor.

In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak.
